securityNotes: Read SKILL.md in full and reviewed all three scripts (snapshot.ts 1469 lines, extract_inline_html.ts 1025 lines, post_process.ts 498 lines) at the pinned SHA -- read fully in editor plus a targeted grep for eval/exec/child_process/process.env/fetch/http.request/apikey/token/credential/curl/wget/download/spawn across all three files. Findings: post_process.ts and extract_inline_html.ts's own top-level code have none of those patterns except extract_inline_html.ts's documented node:http/node:https imports, used only to fetch image URLs the user's own MockPage.jsx already references, for base64 inlining (its stated purpose) -- no arbitrary or hidden endpoints. snapshot.ts's fetch() calls run inside page.evaluate() (i.e. inside the Puppeteer-controlled browser page, same-origin credentials mode) purely to inline the page's own stylesheet/image/font resources -- no exfiltration, no external network calls beyond the target app itself. No eval/exec/child_process/env access, no download-and-execute pattern, no hidden instructions. The auth-script example in SKILL.md documents that a user-supplied script can inject credentials into the Puppeteer session for auth-gated pages, which is expected, disclosed, and user-authored, not embedded in this skill.

proposedEntry.name: extract-static-html
proposedEntry.description: Produces a single self-contained static HTML file from a rendered web page or app screen. Primary path (Strategy A): a Puppeteer script (scripts/snapshot.ts) launches headless Chrome against a running dev server or built app, captures the fully rendered DOM plus live CSSOM rules, inlines all stylesheets and same-origin icon fonts, converts img/srcset/canvas content to base64 data URIs, and strips dev-only script tags/HMR overlays -- works with any framework, supports dark-mode classes, fixed-element removal, full-page height capture, and an optional user-supplied auth script for login-gated pages. Fallback path (Strategy B): a browser-subagent DOM capture for pages needing interaction first. Last-resort path: scripts/extract_inline_html.ts flattens a hand-written React mock component into static HTML via Babel AST parsing, and scripts/post_process.ts inlines that HTML's remaining local image references as base64. Used to capture a specific UI state or produce a portable, shareable snapshot of a page for design handoff, documentation, or further processing.
triggers: save this page as a static self-contained HTML file
capture the rendered UI state of this app
extract standalone HTML from my dev server
share a static snapshot of this page
flatten this React mock into standalone HTML
inputs: a running local dev server URL, or a built app directory
optional React mock component (.jsx) plus its CSS files for the fallback path
optional auth script for login-gated pages
outputs: a single self-contained HTML file with inlined CSS, base64 images/icon-fonts, and no external references
